answer: A canyon sensor market paying for sparrow sightings can require every claimant to reserve a metered inference slot. A signed log binds each kernel run to one account for the epoch, and rewards are capped per slot; splitting a machine into aliases cannot multiply its paid capacity. Ten simultaneous identities need ten leased slots and escrowed fees. A wealthy attacker can still buy capacity, and a dishonest meter can forge logs, so independent operators cross-audit usage and randomly replay submitted work.
